source: RC1 deep review, the coordinator's third batch and ruling of 2026-11-23; RFC 0009 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: A session a tenant switch starts names its root, the session its user's login began (the switched session's root, or that session when it is the login's own), and lives only while the root does: its refresh, the retry within the rotation leeway, and a switch from it each read the root, and a root ended, revoked or gone revokes it and refuses (401 token-revoked). Each such answer writes the root back unchanged with a conditional write, so the root is kept as long as a session that depends on it, and a switch back to the root's tenant begins the root again in its principal's count (IDN-35). A switch reads back the session it created and is refused, ending it, when the store did not keep the root. Such a record is written as format 2, which a reader of format 1 refuses (IDN-31).
guards: login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#a session switched to ends with the login it was switched from
login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#the root is the login's session, however many switches lie between
login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#a retry within the leeway is refused once the root has ended
login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#a gone root ends the session as a revoked one does
login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#a switched session's refreshes keep its root
login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#a store that does not keep the root refuses the switch, and ends the session it started
login:SwitchedSessionRootTest#switching back and forth never pushes out the login

cocache:SessionBoundTest#switching back to the login's tenant keeps the login among the latest
